title: Assigned FTC notice removing the Non-Compete Rule
summary: The assigned February 2026 Federal Register notice removes the FTC’s Non-Compete Rule from the Code of Federal Regulations following court decisions and the agency’s abandonment of appeals.
notes:
The reproduced notice explains the agency’s response to vacatur and distinguishes the Non-Compete Rule from two other rulemaking actions discussed in the same document. Its account concerns federal administrative authority and judicial review of the rule.

Removal of this particular rule is not a holding that every noncompetition agreement is enforceable. The state-law and public-policy inquiries in Hassler remain separate. Use this document to trace which institution acted, the legal basis it described, and the effect of the action. The notebook reports the supplied dated document and has not checked for later developments.

textbookImport.basis: Paraphrase of the actual Fall 2026 course supplement. The source retains its own date and legal context; no current-law verification.

topics.noncompetes: The notice concerns a federal rule, while Hassler concerns judicial treatment of a covenant.
topics.public-policy: It illustrates legislation, agency action, and judicial review as distinct sources.
topics.governing-law: Removing one source of regulation does not answer all remaining validity questions.
